quests.instruction: Anu wakes up fifteen minutes late on a school day. Which choice is the most sensible?
quests.correctAnswer: Do the Essential Steps and Skip the Extras ✔️
options: Hit the Snooze Button Again for Five Minutes 😴
Do the Essential Steps and Skip the Extras ✔️
Leave the House Without Getting Dressed 🧸
quests.hint: Remember which steps really matter when time is short.
quests.explanation: When time is short, the necessary steps come first (washing, dressing, bag), and extras such as a long breakfast or fancy hair can wait. Sleeping more or leaving undressed would not solve anything.
quests.funFact: A school keeps a record of late arrivals so that teachers can spot patterns and help.

quests.instruction: The school bus has just left without Hari. His mother is at work, but his grandmother is at home. What should he do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell Grandmother and Ask for Another Way 🧑
options: Stay Home and Tell Nobody 🏠
Tell Grandmother and Ask for Another Way 🧑
Walk to School Alone Along the Busy Road 🚶
quests.hint: Ask yourself who can help him get to school safely.
quests.explanation: A grown-up can arrange another way to school and let the school know. Walking alone on a main road or hiding it are not safe or sensible.
quests.funFact: A phone call or message to the school lets teachers know a child is safe, even if late.

quests.instruction: Ira is late for class, and the corridor is full of children. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Walk Fast but Do Not Run 🚶
options: Walk Fast but Do Not Run 🚶
Run and Push Through the Crowd 🏃
Wait Until the Corridor Is Empty ⏳
quests.hint: Consider getting there soon without hurting anyone.
quests.explanation: Walking briskly gets her there quickly without bumping into others. Running in a crowded corridor can cause falls, and waiting would make her later.
quests.funFact: Walking on one side of a busy corridor keeps people moving smoothly.

quests.instruction: Neha realises she has left her PE kit at home, and PE is the next lesson. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell Her PE Teacher Before the Lesson 🙋
options: Tell Her PE Teacher Before the Lesson 🙋
Borrow a Friend's Kit Without Asking 👕
Hide in the Toilets Until PE Ends 🚽
quests.hint: Work out who can find a solution.
quests.explanation: Telling the teacher early lets them find a solution, such as spare kit or a different task. Borrowing without asking or hiding creates new problems.
quests.funFact: Schools often keep a box of spare PE items for children who forget their own.

quests.instruction: Karan realises his water bottle is still on the school bus. What is a sensible step?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell the Teacher or Bus Driver 🚌
options: Run Down the Road After the Bus 🏃
Forget It and Say Nothing to Anyone 🤐
Tell the Teacher or Bus Driver 🚌
quests.hint: Work out who can get it back for him.
quests.explanation: The teacher or driver can look for it and return it. Running after a bus is dangerous, and saying nothing means it may be lost.
quests.funFact: Bus and train operators run lost-property offices where forgotten items are kept for a time.

quests.instruction: At the shop, Priya notices she left her money at home when it is time to pay for a notebook. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Put It Back and Come Again with Money 🛍️
options: Slip It into Her Bag and Walk Out 🤫
Put It Back and Come Again with Money 🛍️
Ask a Stranger in the Shop for Money 💸
quests.hint: Remember what is honest and safe.
quests.explanation: Putting it back is honest, and she can return with her money. Taking it without paying is stealing, and asking strangers for money is not safe.
quests.funFact: Shopkeepers will often keep an item aside for a short time if a customer asks politely.

quests.instruction: Meera comes home from school with a headache and feels unwell. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a Grown-up and Rest 🛌
options: Tell a Grown-up and Go Out to Play Anyway 🏃
Do Her Homework Without Telling Anyone 📝
Tell a Grown-up and Rest 🛌
quests.hint: Consider who can help her feel better.
quests.explanation: A grown-up can check how she is feeling and decide what she needs, and rest helps her recover. Hiding it, or going out to play anyway, could make her feel worse.
quests.funFact: Headaches in children can have simple causes, such as tiredness or not drinking enough water.

quests.instruction: Leo had a bad day at school and feels upset when he gets home. What helps?
quests.correctAnswer: Talk to a Family Member About It 🗣️
options: Shut Himself in His Room and Say Nothing 🚪
Talk to a Family Member About It 🗣️
Take It Out on His Brother 😠
quests.hint: Focus on sharing how he feels.
quests.explanation: Talking to someone who cares about him can make a problem feel smaller. Shutting himself away or taking it out on others does not help.
quests.funFact: Talking about a problem can make it feel smaller, because it is no longer carried alone.

quests.instruction: Ira is so tired at bedtime that she wants to climb into bed in her school clothes. What is a sensible choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Do the Short Version: Teeth, Pajamas, Bed 🪥
options: Do the Short Version: Teeth, Pajamas, Bed 🪥
Stay Up Late to Do Every Step Slowly 🌙
Skip Every Single Step and Fall Asleep 🛏️
quests.hint: Consider keeping the most important steps.
quests.explanation: On a very tired night, keeping the short version still looks after her. Skipping everything or staying up late does not.
quests.funFact: A short version of a routine keeps the key steps and drops the extras.

quests.instruction: Two brothers share the bathroom on a busy morning, and Dev must leave in twenty minutes. What helps?
quests.correctAnswer: Agree on Turns and Keep Them Short ⏲️
options: Skip Washing and Run for the Bus 🚌
Agree on Turns and Keep Them Short ⏲️
Lock the Door and Take as Long as He Likes 🔒
quests.hint: Decide how two people can both be ready on time.
quests.explanation: Taking short turns means both are ready on time. Locking the door or skipping washing is unfair or unhelpful.
quests.funFact: A sand timer runs for a fixed time, so it is a simple, fair way to share turns.

quests.instruction: Aanya's shoelace snaps as she is about to leave for school. What is a sensible fix?
quests.correctAnswer: Use Another Pair or a Spare Lace 👟
options: Go Barefoot to School 🦶
Tie the Broken Lace Around Her Ankle 🪢
Use Another Pair or a Spare Lace 👟
quests.hint: Focus on getting safe, comfortable shoes quickly.
quests.explanation: Another pair or a spare lace gets her safely to school. Going barefoot or tying a broken lace round her ankle is unsafe.
quests.funFact: The small plastic tips on the ends of laces, called aglets, stop the ends from fraying.

quests.instruction: Tara has just enough time to either pack her bag or feed the cat before the bus. What is the sensible choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Pack the Bag and Ask Someone to Feed the Cat 🎒
options: Feed the Cat and Leave Her Bag at Home Today 🐈
Pack the Bag and Ask Someone to Feed the Cat 🎒
Skip Both Jobs and Just Hope for the Best 🤞
quests.hint: Decide how both jobs can still be done.
quests.explanation: She needs her bag for school, and a family member can feed the cat. Leaving the bag or skipping both would cause problems.
quests.funFact: Cats are usually fed at set times, so asking a family member to take over keeps the routine.

quests.instruction: Joy has football practice at five o'clock and homework due tomorrow. What is a good plan?
quests.correctAnswer: Start Homework Right After School 📚
options: Start Homework Right After School 📚
Do the Homework After Midnight 🌙
Skip Practice Today 🚫
quests.hint: Remember how to fit both in.
quests.explanation: Starting right after school leaves time for both homework and practice. Skipping practice or leaving homework until midnight does not manage the time well.
quests.funFact: Planning an evening in blocks of time is a skill that helps students and adults alike.

quests.instruction: Ila is invited to a friend's party and a cousin is visiting on the same Saturday. What is a good approach?
quests.correctAnswer: Talk to Her Family About the Timing 🗣️
options: Talk to Her Family About the Timing 🗣️
Say Nothing and Hope It Works Out 🤞
Say Yes to Both and Be Late for Both ⏰
quests.hint: Remember who can help sort out a clash.
quests.explanation: Talking it through may allow her to do both, or to choose kindly. Promising both and being late, or saying nothing, can upset both people.
quests.funFact: Calendars on the fridge help families spot clashes before they happen.

quests.instruction: Dev wants to watch a thirty-minute show, but dinner is in ten minutes. What is the best choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Save It Until After Dinner 🍽️
options: Start It and Make Everyone Wait 🕰️
Watch It at the Table 📺
Save It Until After Dinner 🍽️
quests.hint: Think about how the time fits.
quests.explanation: The show will not fit before dinner, so waiting avoids keeping others waiting. Eating in front of a screen takes attention from the family.
quests.funFact: Recorded or streamed shows can be paused and watched later.

quests.instruction: Sana's aunt and cousin are arriving in an hour. Which job helps the most?
quests.correctAnswer: Tidy the Living Room and Set Out Seats 🛋️
options: Tidy the Living Room and Set Out Seats 🛋️
Start a Long Game in Her Room 🎮
Rearrange Her Whole Bookshelf by Colour 📚
quests.hint: The clue is where guests will spend their time.
quests.explanation: Guests will sit in the living room, so tidying it and setting out seats prepares the space they will use.
quests.funFact: Offering water to a visitor is a customary sign of welcome in India.

quests.instruction: A visitor asks for a glass of water while Dev is in the middle of a video game. What should he do?
quests.correctAnswer: Pause and Bring the Water Politely 🥛
options: Tell Them to Fetch It Themselves 🙄
Ignore the Request Until the Game Ends 🎮
Pause and Bring the Water Politely 🥛
quests.hint: Decide how a guest should feel in his home.
quests.explanation: Pausing shows the guest matters more than the game. Ignoring the request or telling them to fetch it is unwelcoming.
quests.funFact: Most video games can be paused, so a short break costs little.

quests.instruction: The visitors are about to leave. Which kind step should Anu take?
quests.correctAnswer: Say Goodbye and Thank Them for Coming 👋
options: Slip Away to Another Room 🚪
Start Cleaning While They Are Still Talking 🧹
Say Goodbye and Thank Them for Coming 👋
quests.hint: The clue is how guests feel when they leave.
quests.explanation: A warm goodbye and thanks show appreciation. Slipping away or cleaning around guests can seem unfriendly.
quests.funFact: People around the world say goodbye in different ways, from a wave to a bow to a hug.

quests.instruction: Anu is having dinner at a friend's house, and the food is something she has never tried. What is polite?
quests.correctAnswer: Try a Small Taste and Say Thank You 🙏
options: Say It Looks Awful 😖
Try a Small Taste and Say Thank You 🙏
Push It Away Without Saying Anything 🤐
quests.hint: Ask yourself how the cook would feel.
quests.explanation: Trying a little and thanking the cook shows respect. Insulting the food or ignoring it would hurt feelings. If she has an allergy, she should tell the host.
quests.funFact: Trying a new food a few times is one way people grow to like it.

quests.instruction: Rohan sees that everyone takes their shoes off at the door of his friend's house. What should he do?
quests.correctAnswer: Take His Shoes Off Too 👟
options: Keep Them On Because He Does at Home 🚶
Ask Them to Change Their Rule 🙄
Take His Shoes Off Too 👟
quests.hint: Work out whose house it is.
quests.explanation: When visiting, we follow the host's customs. Keeping shoes on or asking for a rule change would be disrespectful.
quests.funFact: A 'genkan' is the small entrance area in a Japanese home where shoes are left.

quests.instruction: At a sleepover, the host family says lights out is at nine. What should Mina do?
quests.correctAnswer: Follow the Host Family's Rules 🌙
options: Follow the Host Family's Rules 🌙
Stay Up Whispering Anyway 🗣️
Go Home Without Telling Anyone 🚪
quests.hint: Remember whose house she is in.
quests.explanation: Following the host's rules respects the family and keeps everyone safe. Staying up or leaving without telling would cause worry.
quests.funFact: In the United States, a sleepover is sometimes called a slumber party.

quests.instruction: The family arrives at the park for a picnic, but it is closed for the day. What is a sensible choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Find Another Place Nearby, Together 🗺️
options: Climb Over the Fence to Get In Anyway 🧗
Find Another Place Nearby, Together 🗺️
Go Home Upset and Say Nothing to Anyone 😠
quests.hint: The clue is how to keep the day going safely.
quests.explanation: Finding another place keeps the outing going and keeps everyone safe. Climbing a fence is dangerous, and going home upset spoils the day.
quests.funFact: Notices at a park gate tell visitors when it is closed and when it will reopen.

quests.instruction: The train is delayed by two hours, and the children are getting bored. What is a good way to pass the time?
quests.correctAnswer: Read or Play a Quiet Game Together 📖
options: Complain Loudly to Other Passengers 😠
Read or Play a Quiet Game Together 📖
Wander Off to Explore Alone 🧭
quests.hint: Think about staying together without disturbing others.
quests.explanation: Quiet activities keep the group together and do not disturb others. Wandering off is unsafe, and complaining loudly bothers people.
quests.funFact: Railway stations have waiting rooms with seats for passengers whose trains are delayed.

quests.instruction: On the way home from a school trip, the bus is very late. What should the children do?
quests.correctAnswer: Wait Together and Tell the Teacher 🚏
options: Wait Together and Tell the Teacher 🚏
Start Walking Home Alone 🚶
Accept a Lift from Someone Nearby 🚗
quests.hint: The key is staying with the group.
quests.explanation: Staying together means the teacher knows where everyone is. Walking alone or accepting a lift from someone nearby is unsafe.
quests.funFact: Teachers count children at the start and end of every trip so that nobody is left behind.

quests.instruction: It is Saturday morning, and Meera's family is sharing out the weekend jobs. Her jobs are to tidy her room and bring her washing downstairs. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Do Her Own Jobs Without Being Reminded 🧺
options: Do Only the Jobs She Enjoys 🎨
Wait Until Someone Reminds Her Three Times 🔔
Do Her Own Jobs Without Being Reminded 🧺
quests.hint: Consider taking responsibility for her own share.
quests.explanation: Doing her own jobs without reminders shows responsibility and helps the family. Waiting to be reminded or choosing only fun jobs leaves others with extra work.
quests.funFact: A weekly chore list can make jobs feel lighter, because everyone knows their share.

quests.instruction: Aanya finishes her jobs early. Which is the most considerate next step?
quests.correctAnswer: Offer to Help Someone Else 🤝
options: Tell Everyone How Quickly She Finished 📣
Offer to Help Someone Else 🤝
Hide So She Is Not Given More Work 🙈
quests.hint: Remember how the rest of the family is getting on.
quests.explanation: Offering to help shares the load and makes the family's work lighter. Hiding or boasting does not.
quests.funFact: Helping others without being asked is often called taking the initiative.

quests.instruction: Hari is asked to look after his little cousin for ten minutes while the adults talk. What should he do?
quests.correctAnswer: Stay with Her and Keep Her Safe 👧
options: Go and Play with His Own Friends 🎮
Leave Her Alone Near the Road 🚗
Stay with Her and Keep Her Safe 👧
quests.hint: Think about who is responsible for her right now.
quests.explanation: Looking after her means staying close and watching her. Leaving her alone near a road or going off to play would put her at risk.
quests.funFact: Young children need an adult or an older child to watch them near roads and water.

quests.instruction: Priya is late for school. Her bag is ready and her shoes are on, but she notices the kitchen tap is dripping. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a Grown-up and Leave on Time ⏰
options: Stay Behind to Try to Fix It Herself 🔧
Leave Without Telling Any Grown-up 🚪
Tell a Grown-up and Leave on Time ⏰
quests.hint: Think about whose job it is, and what she has to do now.
quests.explanation: A dripping tap is a job for a grown-up, so Priya tells one and leaves on time. Fixing it would make her later, and saying nothing leaves the water running.
quests.funFact: Water meters can show that water is flowing even when no tap seems to be open, which helps people spot leaks.

quests.instruction: The family will leave at five o'clock for a wedding. At a quarter to five, Mina is still outside playing in muddy clothes. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Come In, Wash and Change Quickly 🚿
options: Come In, Wash and Change Quickly 🚿
Keep Playing Until She Is Called Twice 🎮
Go in Her Muddy Clothes 👗
quests.hint: Decide how much time is left.
quests.explanation: Fifteen minutes is enough to wash and change if she starts now. Waiting to be called again or going muddy would make her late or untidy.
quests.funFact: Mud is easier to wash out while it is still wet than after it has dried onto fabric.

quests.instruction: Tomorrow the class has an early trip, and rain is forecast. Which plan is best?
quests.correctAnswer: Pack Tonight with a Raincoat 🌧️
options: Pack Tonight with a Raincoat 🌧️
Pack in the Morning and Skip the Raincoat 🌤️
Set a Later Alarm and Rush 🛌
quests.hint: The clue is what the forecast and the early start each call for.
quests.explanation: Packing tonight handles the early start, and a raincoat handles the forecast. Packing in the morning or setting a later alarm would leave too little time.
quests.funFact: Forecasts for the next day are usually fairly reliable, so they are worth checking the evening before.
